requirements.requirement: Repair bin/reconcile so only one invocation processes pending.tsv at a time and a contender receives a clear result.
requirements.summary: The installed script takes a non-blocking flock before reading pending.tsv. A bounded concurrent test directly showed the lock holder active while the contender exited 75 with “reconcile: already running; no work performed.”

requirements.requirement: Preserve existing ledger entries and ensure each pending batch ID reaches ledger.tsv exactly once.
requirements.summary: The initial ledger contained B100. Final observations contained B100, B101, and B102 exactly once each, both before and after restart. Exact fixed-string line matching is used.

requirements.requirement: An interrupted invocation must not permanently block later reconciliation work.
requirements.summary: A lock-owning invocation was terminated and returned 143; the lock then became available and a subsequent reconciliation completed successfully with correct ledger counts.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed OS release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The implementation uses the already-installed util-linux flock 2.40.2 and POSIX shell. RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 were unchanged after execution and restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Exclusive ownership, a clear contention response, exact ledger results, interruption recovery, and platform preservation were directly demonstrated. The provider-wide restart protocol was also strong: node1 was healthy before restart, the restart was acknowledged and accompanied by temporary connection loss, the boot ID changed from 21972395-6444-42bf-8e37-5c3108194a7d to bb0f0d36-3864-4908-a2b8-e11e16378fe5, and system, script, lock, and data health recovered afterward.
limitations: The first attempted concurrency test was malformed by shell working-directory/backgrounding behavior and did not launch its contender successfully (cmd-1594d74f6cdd41e1); the later bounded contention and interruption test corrected this and passed.

The interruption test terminated the invocation while a test wrapper paused immediately after lock acquisition, rather than during the ledger append itself. It nevertheless directly demonstrated automatic lock release and successful later work.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The script and ledger changes directly served the task; the temporary lock-delay wrapper, captured outputs, and backup were bounded test artifacts and were removed. The reboot was required by the provider evidence protocol. Final observations show no failed services, new exposure, package damage, or abandoned executor artifacts.
